paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: This figure compares the error rate (one average minus test accuracy), computation cost, and GPU memory across our approach and baselines, for fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks with QAdapter.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the number of floating point operations per second (FLOPs) required by various methods for fine-tuning using QAdapter on ten NLP tasks. The vertical axis represents the number of FLOPs, labeled as "# FLOPs," and employs a logarithmic scale ranging from \(10^{18}\) to \(10^{20}\). The horizontal axis displays the different methods used for fine-tuning, including "Full FT," "TAG," "Adapter," "MTL-FT," "QAdapter," and "Ours." The bars are predominantly colored in orange, with "Ours" represented by a green bar. The tallest bar corresponds to "Full FT," approximately \(2 \times 10^{20}\) FLOPs, followed by "TAG" and "Adapter," each around \(1.5 \times 10^{20}\) FLOPs. "MTL-FT" shows a lower value close to \(1 \times 10^{19}\) FLOPs, while "QAdapter" and "Ours" illustrate minimal operation requirements, with "Ours" being the shortest at approximately \(5 \times 10^{18}\) FLOPs. The bars are arranged in descending order of FLOPs from left to right, and the emphasized color difference highlights "Ours" as the most efficient method among the compared approaches.
